title: OOM
body:
**Object Oriented Modeling.** Drawing the objects: classes as boxes with their attributes and
operations, and lines between them for the relationships (association, aggregation,
composition, and [[Inheritance]]). UML is the notation the course uses.

It is not a third stage after [[OOA]] and [[OOD]]; it is the notation both of them are
expressed in. [[OOA]] holds the table that keeps the three straight.

The relationships are the part worth reading a diagram for, because they *are* the coupling:
every line is one class knowing about another. See [[Class Relationships]] for the kinds, and
[[Coupling and Cohesion]] for why the count matters.

The general case is [[Modeling]]: a deliberately incomplete picture, cheap to be wrong in and
readable by someone who cannot read code.
